title: Keystone observability matrix + weekly ops cadence
body:
Purpose

This is a working plan for a compact, investigation-first observability surface we call the 'Keystone Matrix'. The goal: a small set of dashboard lanes + metric contracts + trace anchors that let an oncall / SRE / feature owner quickly establish a hypothesis and either escalate or resolve in one investigation pass.

Scope and constraints
- Focus: token inference stacks (model serving + routing + KV cache + request pipeline) but generalize to embeddings and reranking where useful.
- Cost constraint: dashboards must be query-cost-aware; default retention on the keystone lane is 30d, probes/expensive traces pinned to 7d.
- Sampling: adaptive sampling budget (see Sampling heuristics) — default 0.5% trace capture for steady-state, bump to 5% for anomalies flagged by keystone probes.

Keystone Matrix (short summary)
- Lanes: User-Perceived Latency, Token Path Health, KV/Cache Warmth, Model Routing & Fallbacks, Error & Rate Signals, Cost & Throughput.
- Each lane: 3 core metrics + 1 probe + trace anchor.
- Metric contracts below define cardinality, aggregation, and SLO mapping.

Metric definitions (compact)
1) user_ttf_token_ms (User-Perceived Latency)
   - unit: milliseconds (time to first token + median tail calculus)
   - aggregation: p50, p90, p99 by route, model, and tenant (tenant optional for low-volume customers)
   - cardinality: route × region × model_variant; try to keep tenant only for top-20 tenants by volume
   - SLO mapping: p95 < 150ms for interactive routes; p99 < 500ms for background batch routes

2) token_service_tail_ms (Token Path Health)
   - unit: milliseconds per token generation step (captures rotor/attention slowdowns)
   - aggregation: p50/p90/p99 over token lengths buckets (0-128,129-512,512+)
   - trace anchor: attach span ids for slow-token-path with KV-hit flag

3) kv_warmth_index (KV/Cache Warmth)
   - unit: ratio (0-1) representing fraction of prefix requests served from local KV
   - aggregation: average per node pool and 95th percentile across tenants
   - alert heuristic: sudden drop > 15% sustained for 10 minutes -> investigate prefetch/evictions

4) route_fallback_rate (Model Routing & Fallbacks)
   - unit: ratio per 1000 requests (fallbacks/requests)
   - aggregation: rate per route and per region; include fallback reason tag (capacity, timeout, error)
   - trace anchor: when fallback occurs, annotate request span with chosen model_variant and upstream latency

5) request_error_budget_use (Error & Rate Signals)
   - unit: percentage of SLO violations consumed vs budgeted for the period
   - aggregation: daily cadence; rollups per product team that own route

6) token_cost_perk (Cost & Throughput)
   - unit: cost in $ per 1k tokens (approx), normalized by model family and quantization profile
   - aggregation: rolling 24h average by model, with throughput buckets (low/med/high)

Trace design notes
- Trace anchors: each lane includes a canonical trace field list (request_id, route, model_variant, tenant_id, kv_hit, gpu_node, kernel_version). Keep the schema small.
- Sampling: add adaptive rule to increase sampling for request_error_budget_use violation and kv_warmth_index dips.
- Span naming: standardized patterns: span.infer.<model_variant>, span.kv.lookup, span.router.decision, span.compile.kernel-select.
- Trace size budget: aim for 8-12 spans per sampled request (strip internal debug-only spans unless investigation mode).

Dashboard composition rules (how to build a keystone lane tile)
- Tile composition: a top-line metric (quantile) + small multi-series sparkline for last 6h + cohort breakdown dropdown (route/model/region).
- Drillthrough: every top-line tile links directly to a minimal investigation view pre-filtered by the same cohort — includes relevant traces and a short checklist (Check KV, Check routing, Check recent rollouts).
- Color/alerting: use banded thresholds (yellow warning, orange critical) tied to SLOs; avoid noisy up/down blips by requiring a 3-sample hold for alerts (configurable).

Investigation checklist template (one-click exported from tile)
- Confirm scope (route/model/region/time window)
- Look at user_ttf_token_ms quantile curve + token_service_tail_ms breakdown by token bucket
- Check kv_warmth_index for warm/cold patterns
- Check route_fallback_rate and any recent rollout flags or canary changes (linked PRs)
- If fallback or error: open traces for 5 slow/error cases; note kernel version & probe flags; escalate if same gpu_node repeatedly appears

Weekly ops cadence (proposed minimal ritual)
- Monday quicksync (30m): pass through keystone lane anomalies from weekend, owner assignments. Required: ops lead + 2 oncall engineers + 1 product owner.
- Wednesday triage (60m): deep-dive on top 3 recurring anomalies; action items for instrumentation or rollbacks. Invite model owners when routing/fallbacks show shifts.
- Friday cleanup (30m): review probes and sampling rates, archive stale metrics or reduce retention on low-value panels.

Playbook for adding a new metric to the keystone lane
1) Author creates a short PR with metric name, unit, tags, and a one-line SLO proposal. Link a short experiment query and expected cost (monthly).
2) Run a 2-week shadow experiment with dashboard off by default; collect operator feedback.
3) If useful, add to lane with sampling guidance and trace anchor. If noisy -> stash to 'experiment deck' and revisit next quarter.

Open questions / TODOs
- Host-level vs route-level cardinality: need policy to automatically roll tenants into sampling when low-volume; define the top-tenant cutoff.
- Decide exact adaptive-sampling thresholds and ramp rules for large-scale bursts.
- Integrate with rollout automation: link rollout tags to route_fallback_rate so rollouts surface automatically on the keystone lane.

Quick links and references
- JIRA-OBS-4821: Adaptive sampling prototype
- CONFLUENCE-OBS-1342: Dashboard UX sketch (internal)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/obs-dashboards/pull/268 (proposed lane widgets)

Notes to self / rough edits
- Keep the keystone lane intentionally small — mental load is the enemy.
- For multi-model fanout, always surface the per-variant fallback tag (helps correlate cost spikes).
- Consider a compact 'operator quickcard' that auto-populates fields (tenant, route, window) for postmortem templates.

If you want to iterate: attach example queries you ran, and I will fold them into the experiment appendix.
